translation_notes: both RDF operations of the region are absorbed: RDF.type -> rdf:type and Variable('CLASS') -> the variable island ?CLASS. The returned tuple is a SPARQL-ish triple pattern, and ldpy lets it be written with SPARQL's own notation while staying an ordinary Python tuple.
the mechanical draft only rewrote RDF.type and left Variable('CLASS') alone; the variable island is exactly the kind of term this region is made of, so it was applied by hand

the mechanical draft also inserted the @prefix statements inside the parenthesised `from rdflib import (...)` list, which is a syntax error; they were moved after the import, and the unused rdfs: declaration was dropped
RDF and Variable become dead names in the rdflib import line on the ldpy side; the line is left untouched (shared preamble of the enclosing module)
driver: a stand-in `self` supplies the single attribute the region reads (identifier); the harness compares the returned 3-tuple term by term. Two fixtures, a named class and a blank-node class.
